xrefdescription.para: CTI-01 — stop() called immediately after start() must return within kSchedulerStopTimeout and leave isRunning() == false.
CTI-02 — Repeated stop + start cycles are stable; the scheduler can be restarted after every stop without crashing or leaking resources.
CTI-03 — Entries added with scheduleIn() when the scheduler is STOPPED are added to the pending queue but MUST NOT fire until start() is called.

simplesect.para: chaos_contract.h § 6 — scheduleIn() on STOPPED scheduler may queue entry

xrefdescription.para: CTI-04 — Calling start() while the scheduler is already running is idempotent: it must not launch a second worker thread or crash.

simplesect.para: chaos_contract.h § 6 — start() on RUNNING is idempotent

xrefdescription.para: CTI-05 — Calling stop() when the scheduler has never been started (or has already been stopped) must be a no-op without throwing.

simplesect.para: chaos_contract.h § 6 — stop() on STOPPED is idempotent

xrefdescription.para: CTI-06 — With WakeStrategy::CONDVAR, stop() completes within themis::chaos::kSchedulerStopTimeout regardless of tick_interval.
CTI-07 — With WakeStrategy::FIXED_TICK, a scheduled fault fires within the expected deadline (delay + 3 × tick_interval as headroom).
CTI-08 — Two independent ChaosScheduler instances (one FIXED_TICK, one CONDVAR) running concurrently inject into separate FaultInjectors without interfering with each other.

briefdescription.para: Phase 4 resilience regression tests for ChaosScheduler timing race conditions.

detaileddescription.para: Covers eight test cases mapped to chaos roadmap Phase 4 hardening:

para.heading: CTI — Chaos Timing and Interface Regressions

detaileddescription.para: CTI-01 stop() called immediately after start() — no deadlock, isRunning() returns false CTI-02 Restart (stop + start) cycle repeated N times — stable, no resource leak CTI-03 scheduleIn() called after stop() — entry is queued but not fired CTI-04 start() called while scheduler already running — idempotent, single worker thread CTI-05 stop() on a STOPPED scheduler is idempotent — no exception, no crash CTI-06 CONDVAR wake strategy: stop() latency is bounded within kSchedulerStopTimeout CTI-07 FIXED_TICK wake strategy: fault fires within expected tick window CTI-08 Mixed wake strategies: two independent schedulers run concurrently without interference
